context:
### SOURCE [1] Google Willow (https://blog.google/technology/research/google-willow-quantum-chip/)
In December 2024 Google announced Willow, a 105-qubit superconducting quantum chip (Nature paper published Dec 9, 2024). It performed a random circuit sampling benchmark in under five minutes; Google estimates the same task would take Frontier, one of today's fastest supercomputers, about 10 septillion (10^25) years - longer than the age of the universe. Willow also showed that errors can be reduced exponentially as more qubits are added (below-threshold error correction). The benchmark has no practical use by itself.
### SOURCE [2] NIF fusion ignition (https://www.aip.org/fyi/2022/national-ignition-facility-achieves-long-sought-fusion-goal)
On December 5, 2022 the National Ignition Facility at Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory delivered 2.05 megajoules of laser energy to a fuel target and got 3.15 megajoules of fusion energy out - the first controlled fusion experiment to produce more energy from the target than the lasers put in ('ignition'). The lasers needed about 300 megajoules of electricity from the grid, so it was not net electricity gain. A July 30, 2023 shot reached 3.88 MJ.
### SOURCE [3] Casgevy CRISPR therapy (https://www.statnews.com/2023/12/08/fda-approves-casgevy-crispr-based-medicine-for-treatment-of-sickle-cell-disease/)
On December 8, 2023 the US FDA approved Casgevy, the first approved therapy in the US that uses CRISPR gene editing, for sickle cell disease in patients 12 and older; UK regulators had approved it shortly before (November 2023). Patients' own blood stem cells are edited outside the body with CRISPR-Cas9 and infused back.
### SOURCE [4] Neuralink (https://www.cbsnews.com/amp/news/elon-musk-neuralink-human-trials-mouse)
Neuralink implanted its brain-computer interface in its first human patient in January 2024. In February 2024 the company said the patient could move a computer cursor just by thinking. The patient, Noland Arbaugh, was paralyzed from the shoulders down after a diving accident; a company demo showed him playing chess on a computer using only his thoughts.
